# named fields and enforces every other one.

Every other field is enforced and agrees for the whole trace

D14 waives `position`: finetune 14 on every sample, so the continuous-versus-table period drifts about a quarter of a source frame per tick (first at tick 3 channel 3, 12 against 14). Every other field, including the Amiga-limit clamp, is enforced and agrees for the whole trace

D14 waives `position`: `PatternJump.mod` uses finetune 14 on both samples (first drift at tick 14 channel 2, 1744 against 1746). The `Bxx` overriding `Dxx` behaviour this fixture exists to test is enforced and agrees, including order, row and the active set

D14 waives `position`: `InstrSwapRetrigger.mod` uses finetunes 7 and 8 (first drift at tick 3 channel 0, 663 against 665). The C2a D18 adapter projection removed the old row 1 frame 8 alignment error; the E9x retrigger and instrument swap themselves are enforced and agree

D14 waives `position`: C2a research point 2 resolved — this is not a `9xx` retained-pointer difference and not a loop gate. `ptoffset.mod` uses finetune 14; the offsets applied at ticks 0 to 7 match exactly and the first drift is tick 8 channel 0, 4560 against 4562. Every other field, active set included, is enforced and agrees

D14 waives `position`: `PTInstrSwap.mod` uses finetune-14 samples, so the continuous-versus-table period drifts (first drift at tick 9 channel 0, 1407 against 1409). The D12 queued lone-instrument replacement this fixture exists to test now lands at the loop boundary and every other field, the row 12 empty-slot null sample included, is enforced and agrees for the whole trace

D14 waives `position`: libxmp's rounded C-4 rate makes its clock 8287 x 428 = 3_546_836 Hz against the exact PAL 3_546_895 Hz, 17 ppm, which crosses the one-integer-sample bound only at the final compared tick 383 channel 0 (19 against 21). Every other field is enforced and agrees
D16: PT's flat-table zero period retains volume 64 where libxmp silences the voice. First divergence at tick 1 channel 0 field volume: expected 0, actual 64
D17: this oracle requests the non-ProTracker default sample-change profile. First divergence at tick 6 channel 0 field instrument: expected 1, actual 2

D21, on top of the D15 CIA-latch waiver of `frame` and `position`. Every other field is enforced, and the trace diverges at tick 6 channel 0 field active: ProTracker's `mt_RetrigNote` retriggers on tick zero of a row that carries `E9x` and no note, so StarPlayer keeps restarting the 672-frame one-shot, while libxmp handles retrigger only from tick one, lets the sample run out during row 1 tick 0 and drops the channel for the rest of the module

D15 waives `frame` and `position` for the CIA-latch reason. Every other field is enforced and the whole trace now agrees: the tick 136 channel 0 volume difference was the signed-shift LFO rounding corrected by C3b

D18, not D12: the queued tone-portamento replacement now lands. The remaining divergence is at tick 37 channel 0 field active — row 7's empty instrument slot queues ProTracker's null sample, whose stop falls due inside the interval, so libxmp omits the channel for that whole tick while C1 snapshots the voice at the boundary before it. The D18 projection covers only a one-shot running out, not a queued stop on a looping voice

D22, not D12: the queued replacement lands and `position` stays waived for D14 finetune drift (first drift at tick 19 channel 0, 2992 against 2994). The remaining divergence is at tick 150 channel 1 field instrument, expected 1 against actual 2 — row 25's `ED3` row. ProTracker latches the instrument column at tick zero and defers only the DMA restart, while libxmp defers the whole event to the delay tick, so the two disagree about the reported instrument for the three ticks before the note fires

D12 is implemented and the queued replacement now lands; `position` is waived for the single tick where the channel is revived. libxmp keeps its ended voice mapped and reports that voice's parked position (250) for the tick in which it hot-swaps, while C1 reports the replacement StarPlayer starts at the same event boundary (0). Every following tick, active set and instrument included, agrees exactly

D18, not D12: the queued replacement now lands and exactly one tick of 343 differs. At tick 295 channel 0 the queued one-shot-behind-one-shot stop falls due *inside* the interval, so libxmp omits the channel for the whole tick while C1 snapshots the voice still sounding at the boundary before it. The adapter's D18 one-shot projection cannot recognise it because the channel's reported sample is already the queued replacement, whose length the projection tests instead
